opera: Oslo's Opera House is a great building of white marble and glass that slopes down into the water of the fjord: you walk on the sloping roof as if it were a square, and from the top you see the whole city and the harbour. Around it are the new Bjørvika districts.
munch: The museum devoted to Edvard Munch, in a glass-and-steel tower on the harbour: it holds the world's largest collection of his work, including versions of "The Scream" and "Vampire". The upper floors have fine views of the fjord and the Opera.
akershus: The medieval fortress that has guarded the harbour for over seven hundred years: ramparts, cannons, the castle and wide views over the fjord. You can walk the walls and courtyards without a ticket.
radhuset: The red-brick building with two square towers on the harbour, where the Nobel Peace Prize is awarded every 10 December. Inside, the halls are covered in large paintings and frescoes about Norwegian history and life.
slottet: Karl Johans gate and the Royal Palace
Oslo's main street, running from the station up to the Royal Palace on the hill, past the Parliament and the National Theatre. The palace is surrounded by a public park where you can walk freely.
vigeland: A large park with over two hundred bronze and granite sculptures by Gustav Vigeland: people of all ages, embraces, games and the Monolith, a column of a hundred and twenty intertwined figures. A favourite strolling spot for Oslo's residents.
nasjonal: Scandinavia's largest art museum, in a new building on the harbour next to City Hall: Norwegian and international painting, design, architecture and a room of Munch's works. It's one of the places where a version of "The Scream" is kept.
brygge: Aker Brygge, Tjuvholmen and the Nobel Peace Center

Oslo's modern waterfront, with the old shipyard quays turned into bars, shops and squares on the water. Further on, Tjuvholmen has art galleries and outdoor sculptures. Next to it is the Nobel Peace Center.
fram: Fram Museum and the Bygdøy peninsula

The museum of the polar ship Fram, which took the Norwegian explorers Nansen and Amundsen to the North and South Poles: you go aboard the real ship, in a large tent-shaped building. The Bygdøy peninsula also has other maritime museums and the Kon-Tiki Museum.
holm: Holmenkollen: the ski jump and ski museum
The famous ski jump on Oslo's northern hill, with the world's oldest ski museum and a tower with views over the whole city and the fjord. Half an hour from the centre by metro.
grun: Oslo's liveliest neighbourhood, of cafés, independent shops and murals. Along the Akerselva river, past old mills and waterfalls, you reach Mathallen, the food hall with some thirty Norwegian and international food stalls.
